sources.entry: CmdIME - Input source switcher that gives each input source its own key, such as Left Command for English and Right Command for Chinese.

summary.one_liner: CmdIME is a macOS input-source switcher that binds each installed input source to its own modifier key or shortcut, such as Left Command for English and Right Command for Chinese.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you assign a single tap, double tap, or shortcut (for example Option+J) to each input source on your Mac, and selects that source directly. After a switch it checks that macOS actually changed sources and retries if not. It shows a small indicator near the text caret with eighteen built-in themes, including Glass and Liquid Glass, plus custom themes and fonts. It can also set input sources per app, per website (reading only the address of the front page in Safari or Chrome), and per terminal program, with Herdr noted as the best-supported terminal. A command-line tool, keyboardctl, handles scanning, binding, switching, rules, export/import and diagnostics.
use_cases: switch between English and Chinese input with one key
assign a dedicated key to each keyboard language on macOS
show which input source is active near the cursor
set different input sources for different apps or websites
switch input source from a script or editor integration
diagnose why an input source switch failed
notable: Each key always selects the same input source, unlike Control+Space which cycles or toggles
Verifies that macOS applied the switch and retries when it did not
Per-app, per-website, and per-terminal-program input source rules
Eighteen built-in indicator themes plus custom JSON themes and fonts
Toggle trigger that flips between two chosen slots
caveats: Requires macOS 13 or later on Apple silicon; Intel Macs are not supported yet
Preview build that is signed but not notarized, so a browser-downloaded zip is blocked by Gatekeeper
Needs Accessibility and Input Monitoring permissions to listen for keys
Per-program switching works best in Herdr; other terminals switch only when a program starts or exits
